en: Udāna 4.3 Gopālakasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering on tour among the Kosalans together with a large community of monks.
Then the Blessed One, having stepped down from the road, approached a certain tree root; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Then a certain cowherd approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
As the cowherd sat there to one side, the Blessed One instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dhamma.
Then, having been instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s discourse on the Dhamma, the cowherd said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, accept my meal for tomorrow.”
The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.
Then that cowherd, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him to his right, departed.
Then, at the end of that night, the cowherd had plenty of rice porridge with little water prepared in his own residence, along with fresh ghee, and announced it was time for the Blessed One.
“Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, went together with the community of monks to the residence of that cowherd; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Then that cowherd, with his own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with rice porridge mixed with little water and fresh ghee.
Then, when the Blessed One had finished his meal and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, that cowherd took a certain low seat and sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dhamma; then, rising from his seat, he departed.
Not long after the Blessed One had left, a certain man deprived that cowherd of life at the boundary between two districts.

Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. As they were sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

"Venerable sir, that cowherd by whom today the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha was personally satisfied and served with rice porridge with little water and fresh ghee—it is said, venerable sir, that this cowherd has been [confronted] by a certain man..."
“...was deprived of life by Sīmantarikā.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Whatever one might do from region to region...”
Or even an enemy toward an enemy—
it is a mind wrongly directed that makes one worse than that.
The third.
